sentences.text: Akialoa is an extinct genus of Hawaiian honeycreepers belonging to the subfamily Carduelinae within the family Fringillidae.
The Oʻahu, Maui Nui, and Kauaʻi ʻakialoa were once grouped together as a single species known as the greater ʻakialoa.
The Oʻahu ʻakialoa (Akialoa ellisiana) was confirmed extinct in 1837, though an unconfirmed extinction date of 1940 exists.
The Maui Nui ʻakialoa (Akialoa lanaiensis) went extinct in 1892.
The Lesser ʻakialoa (Akialoa obscura) is recorded as extinct in 1940.
The Kauaʻi ʻakialoa (Akialoa stejnegeri) went extinct in 1969.
The Hoopoe-billed ʻakialoa (Akialoa upupirostris) is known to be extinct during the Holocene epoch.
A Giant ʻakialoa (Akialoa sp.) is recorded as extinct during the Holocene epoch.
The genus Akialoa was described by Olson and James in 1995.
All species of Akialoa are extinct and formerly lived throughout the Hawaiian islands. Akialoa lived from the Gelasian to the Late Pleistocene, approximately 2.58 to 0.0117 million years ago.
